newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola chief indicted in union effort.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola chief indicted in union effort.

text.p: James Wardlaw, a vice president with Coca-Cola Enterprises in Atlanta, was named in a five-count federal indictment on Tuesday, his attorney, Charles Fels, said.

Neither Fels nor Wardlaw could immediately be reached for comment, but a release Fels issued said the charges involved a failed attempt by the Bakery, Confectionery and Tobacco Workers Union to organise at Coca-Cola's Atlanta unit in 1994.

The New York Times on Wednesday said the charges were based on allegations that Wardlaw and Eric Turpin, vice president of human resources at the Atlanta unit, bribed a worker to weaken a unionization effort that year.

The report said Wardlaw and Turpin are accused of paying a company truck driver $10,000 and offering him a promotion in exchange for his help in getting his co-workers to vote against Local 42 of the union in an Aug. 3, 1994, election.
The report said the union lost the election.
Wardlaw and Turpin were both charged with five felony counts, including charges of conspiracy and bribery, the paper said.
"Jimmy Wardlaw gave absolutely nothing to anyone to influence the outcome of that election," Fels said in his statement. "We look forward to a rigorous cross-examination of his accuser."
